listeNoel.modesDesc: The twelve questions are the same. With two of you, each answers for themselves, and the quiz tells you which of Santa's lists your couple is on... and which of you is the nicer one.
listeNoel.modeDuoMeta: Your couple's list, and the nicer of the two
listeNoel.setupTitreDuo: Naughty or nice, the two of you?
listeNoel.setupDescDuo: Enter your first names. The first one answers the twelve questions, passes the phone, and the second one takes their turn, each for themselves. At the end you'll know which of Santa's lists your couple is on, and which of you is the nicer one.
listeNoel.setupTitreSolo: Naughty or nice, the two of you?
listeNoel.setupDescSolo: Twelve questions about your December: the advent calendar, the hidden presents, the last Christmas cookie... Answer with the two of you in mind, and find out which list Santa has put you on.
listeNoel.resLibelleDuo: Your niceness score as a couple
listeNoel.quiTitre: Who's the nicer of the two?
listeNoel.duoEgal: A tie: {{valeur}} each. Santa puts you in the same pile.
listeNoel.ecartsTitre: Where one of you was nicer than the other
listeNoel.invitationDuo: And your other half, naughty or nice? Take the quiz again together: you each answer for yourself, and you'll find out which of you brings the average down.
listeNoel.noteFin: This quiz is a game, just for fun. The real Santa hasn't given us access to his lists.
listeNoel.modeDuoDesc: You each answer the twelve questions on the same phone, without seeing the other's answers.
listeNoel.modeSolo: On my own, for the two of us
listeNoel.modeSoloDesc: You answer with the two of you in mind.
listeNoel.relaisDebut: Answer the twelve questions, then pass the phone.
listeNoel.relaisSuite: {{nom}} is done. Your turn, no peeking at their answers!
listeNoel.r1_d: No doubt about it this time. The advent calendar didn't last ten days, the presents were opened early and the last cookie vanished in the kitchen. Santa has set aside two fine lumps of coal, and he wrapped them himself.
listeNoel.r1_a: The good news is that you're made for each other. And apparently coal with a nice ribbon makes very trendy decor.
listeNoel.r2_d: Santa has raised an eyebrow more than once. Last-minute presents, shaken boxes, the couch before dessert... You make everyone laugh at the table, but the elves write everything down.
listeNoel.r2_a: All is not lost: one nicely wrapped present and the dishes done together can still save your Christmas.
listeNoel.r3_d: The elves can't make up their minds. One day you leave the last cookie for the other one, the next day the box of chocolates disappears. Your file has been going back and forth between the two piles since the start of the month.
listeNoel.r3_a: You still have a few days to tip the scales. Breakfast in bed or doing the dishes without being asked counts double in December!
listeNoel.r4_d: You're on it, fair and square. There are two or three slips in your file (a shaken box, one chocolate too many), but nothing that deserves coal. On the whole you look out for each other, and Santa has noticed.
listeNoel.r4_a: The sleigh will stop at your place. To climb a little higher, look below at what was written down.
listeNoel.r5_d: Santa found nothing to complain about. The advent calendar is opened one day at a time, the presents have been ready since November and the last cookie always goes to the other one. You're the couple the elves hold up as an example in workshop meetings.
listeNoel.r5_a: Keep it up, but save one small bit of mischief for next year. A couple that's too good ends up worrying the elves!
listeNoel.q1a: One door a day, not one more
listeNoel.q1b: Two or three doors ahead on rough days
listeNoel.q1d: Empty, and the other one's has been started
listeNoel.q2: The presents are hidden somewhere in your home:
listeNoel.q2a: No snooping, the surprise comes first
listeNoel.q2b: No snooping, but the hiding place has been spotted
listeNoel.q2c: A box or two got shaken
listeNoel.q2d: Everything was opened, then neatly rewrapped
listeNoel.q3: The other one's present was bought:
listeNoel.q3a: In November, and it's already wrapped
listeNoel.q3c: On the evening of the 23rd, at a run
listeNoel.q3d: On the 24th at 6 pm, at a gas station
listeNoel.q4a: Right down to the last ornament, with Christmas music on
listeNoel.q4b: The ornaments, yes. Untangling the lights, no
listeNoel.q4c: Two ornaments hung, then the couch
listeNoel.q4d: Showing up when it's all done, to say it's leaning
listeNoel.q5: The box of chocolates from Grandma:
listeNoel.q5a: One chocolate after dinner, when the box goes around
listeNoel.q5b: Two or three, on the way past
listeNoel.q5c: The top layer was gone in one evening
listeNoel.q5d: It's empty, with the wrappers put back inside
listeNoel.q6a: Paper, ribbon, tag, and nice sharp folds
listeNoel.q6b: Paper, and a lot of tape
listeNoel.q6c: The store bag, with a bow on it
listeNoel.q6d: The other one wraps everything, and both names are on the tag
listeNoel.q7: You had agreed on $50 per present, tops:
listeNoel.q8a: Clearing the table, drying the dishes, serving everyone seconds
listeNoel.q8b: Offering to help while hoping they'll say no
listeNoel.q8c: Staying at the table: someone has to keep them company
listeNoel.q9: Your uncle brings up that touchy subject again:
listeNoel.q9a: Changing the subject while serving dessert
listeNoel.q9b: Staring very closely at the plate
listeNoel.q9c: Slipping in one little remark, just one
listeNoel.q9d: Stirring things up, just to see
listeNoel.q10: The present received is a total miss:
listeNoel.q10a: A big smile, and it will get used at least once
listeNoel.q10b: A thank you, then the back of a closet
listeNoel.q10c: Exchanged on the 26th, without a word
listeNoel.q11c: Taken, since everyone was told to help themselves
listeNoel.q11d: Eaten in the kitchen, no witnesses
listeNoel.q12a: Little thoughtful gestures all year long
listeNoel.q12b: Good times, and two or three slip-ups
